summary: Man on Wire is a 2008 British-American biographical documentary directed by James Marsh about Philippe Petit's 1974 high-wire walk between the Twin Towers of New York's World Trade Center. It is based on Petit's book "To Reach the Clouds", released in paperback as "Man on Wire". The film is structured like a heist film, combining rare preparation footage, photographs, re-enactments and present-day interviews with participants.
one_line: A 2008 British-American documentary by James Marsh chronicling Philippe Petit's 1974 high-wire walk between the World Trade Center Twin Towers.
key_facts: Man on Wire is a 2008 British-American biographical documentary film directed by James Marsh.
The film chronicles Philippe Petit's 1974 high-wire walk between the Twin Towers of New York's World Trade Center.
The film is based on Philippe Petit's book "To Reach the Clouds".
The book "To Reach the Clouds" was released in paperback with the title "Man on Wire".
The film's title is taken from the police report that led to the arrest of Philippe Petit.
Philippe Petit was later released after his arrest following the walk.
Petit's performance on the wire had lasted for almost one hour.
The film is crafted like a heist film.
The film presents rare footage of the preparations for the walk and still photographs of the walk itself.
The film includes re-enactments with Paul McGill playing the young Philippe Petit.
The film includes present-day interviews with participants in the walk.
Barry Greenhouse, an insurance executive, served as the inside man for the walk.
The walk took place in 1974 between the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York.
